Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask, happy to coordinate. Quick answers up front and then details below.

- We retain request logs, admin/audit events (RBAC changes, user invites), and tenant_event_stream entries (model invocation metadata). Canonical export format: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) with per-event ISO-8601 timestamps.
- Default retention for hosted accounts is 13 months (390 days). We have documented retention exceptions (legal holds) that prevent lifecycle deletion; exceptions are applied per-tenant via an approvals workflow.
- Customer access: we support two delivery options: (1) cross-account S3 role for ongoing access (preferred for integrations) and (2) one-off export delivered as a presigned S3 URL / Drive link. Both exports include a manifest CSV (filename, sha256, bytes, first_timestamp, last_timestamp).
- We can produce a 7-day sample extract and manifest by EOD Wed. Rishi will generate the sample from production and Neha will attach the manifest and steps.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the tenant/time window you want (e.g., rolling 7 days ending 2026-11-29).
2) Tell us preferred handoff: cross-account role OR presigned export link.
3) We will provide: NDJSON sample + sample-log-manifest.csv + short export playbook (s3-export-steps.txt).

I'll schedule delivery and include the SIG question IDs in our follow-up once you send them. Looping in Neha for the technical details and Rishi for generation.

Best,

Hi Asha / Marissa,

Details to map to SIG items (QA friendly):

1) Log types & format
- request-logs.ndjson: per-request entries with fields {timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, model, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, status_code}.
- admin-audit.ndjson: RBAC changes, API key events, config changes with actor metadata.
- tenant-event-stream.ndjson: higher-level streaming events (cache hits, KV cache eviction, batching events).

2) Retention & lifecycle
- Default: 390 days (13 months). Lifecycle is implemented via object-store lifecycle policies that transition to Glacier-like storage after 90 days and expire at 390 days.
- Legal hold: flag on tenant metadata prevents lifecycle expiration; removal requires approval from Compliance (audit trail maintained).
- Deletion proof: we can produce a deletion manifest showing lifecycle action logs (service-side events) for a tenant when requested as evidence.

3) Customer access patterns
- Cross-account role: we create an IAM role that BrightBank can assume; role scoped to tenant prefix (s3://redwood-audit-exports/brightbank/<tenant-id>/). This provides ongoing access and respects KMS-encryption.
- One-off export: we generate a staged export and provide a presigned URL valid 7 days. Exports include sample-log-manifest.csv with sha256 checksums.

4) Export/playbook & sample contents
- We'll include s3-export-steps.txt (CLI snippet & permission map), and a small sample (redwood-audit-sample-20261130.ndjson, ~12 MB). Format is NDJSON; each line is a JSON event.

CLI snippet (example):
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports/brightbank/<tenant-id>/20261124-20261130/ ./ --recursive --profile brightbank-access

NOTE: All logs are encrypted at rest with KMS CMKs managed by Redwood; cross-account role requires kms:Decrypt grants.

I'll attach the sample manifest and the steps in my follow-up; Rishi will drop the sample file into the shared drive.

- Neha
